summary: Slice 9 (MCP and OAuth resource-server hardening) is complete: same-origin Origin enforcement added to the Streamable HTTP server config, and the full slice-9 condition set (Streamable HTTP lifecycle, protected-resource metadata/challenge, nine tool schemas, claim failure cases, bounded metadata/JWKS caching with key-rotation overlap, provider-outage-safe errors, rate limits, optional DPoP advertisement) is proven by 291/291 Rust tests and all 4 black-box protocol/security self-tests.
defects: docs/MCP-PRODUCTION-FIX-PLAN.md (referenced by the slice-9 acceptance criteria) does not exist in the repository; the stand-in remediation docs are docs/plans/mcp-production-remediation/ (01-07) plus docs/MCP-PRODUCTION-SUCCESSFUL-COMMANDS-2026-10-09.md. Reported, not papered over.
follow_up: Release is under manual hold: the per-slice continuation gate is preserved and live environment/client/operator input is required before any production release; the SQLite migration does not authorize production changes.
important_context: Slice 9 is complete and verified: 291/291 Rust tests pass (227 lib + 4 main + 12 e2e + 38 integration + 10 transport_host_regression) and all 4 black-box self-tests pass (verify.js, verify-discovery.js, verify-oauth-lifecycle.js, verify-security-isolation.js, all exit 0).

Origin enforcement is same-origin only: allowed_origins is derived from the MCP resource URL's own origin (e.g. https://mcal.hajnal.space); a cross-origin web client would need its origin added via config, not code.

Rate limiting is a fixed window keyed by user_id:client_id, controlled by MCP_RATE_LIMIT_MAX (60), MCP_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS (60), MCP_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED; denial returns JSON-RPC -2004 'rate limit exceeded'.
Provider outage maps TokenError::InvalidToken to a static safe 401 (invalid_token / 'invalid authorization token'); internal detail is only logged via tracing::warn!, never returned.

All slice-9 code changes are uncommitted (no commits per stage contract); oauth.rs (bounded metadata/JWKS caching + key-rotation overlap) is part of the slice-9 work but was already committed in a prior session.
The 2026-10-08 SQLite decision supersedes PostgreSQL hosting for the mcp-server.
